subject: general
question: A kite is soaring at an altitude of 75 meters above the ground, with its string temporarily secured to a point on the ground. The angle of elevation of the string relative to the ground is 30 degrees. Given that the string remains taut, what is the length of the string?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the sides opposite to the angles are always in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The altitude is opposite to the 30° angle, which corresponds to 1 unit = 75 m.

The string acts as the hypotenuse (opposite to 90°), which corresponds to 2 units.

Length of string = 2 × 75 m = 150 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 150 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Altitude of the kite from the ground (Perpendicular, KG) = 75 m

Angle of elevation of the string (θ) = 30°

Let the length of the string (Hypotenuse, KP) be L.

**Formula Used:**

sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

⇒ sin(30°) = KG ÷ KP

⇒ 1/2 = 75 ÷ L

⇒ L = 75 × 2

⇒ L = 150 m

**∴ The correct answer is 150 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios Trick

In any right-angled triangle with angles measuring 30°, 60°, and 90°, the lengths of the sides opposite to these respective angles are strictly in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an observer looks at an object situated above the horizontal line of sight.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse length is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the base and perpendicular. H² = P² + B².
